bayts.text: Weeping is due for departed masters: the earths weep over them as do the heavens.
I weep over them and hope, in weeping, for tomorrow the good pleasure of Him in Whom they lost themselves with sweetness.
Alas, my soul, for the loss of the great ones who have departed to a Lord Who called them to the heights!
The nights and the months together weep over them, like the evenings and the mornings, with longing.
They were servants of their Lord through acts of obedience, and He – exalted be He – was for them a Lord of favours.
They counted the neglect of the litany (wird), like satiety even on lawful food, among the causes of misfortunes.
When the night let down its curtain of darkness, they rose swiftly to bring the deep darkness to life.
They sold the superfluous for the remembrance of Allah, their Creator, and the sleep of the night they sold for intimate converse.
By night their sides forsake their beds (Qurʾān 32:16), forgetful of Salmā and Laylā for the glad tidings.
And wherever Laylā appeared in her splendour, they turned away from her toward the Lord with acts of obedience.
They forget Laylā and Suʿdā in their night vigil, finding intimacy in invocations and verses.
Their talk is the remembrance of the Enricher (Al-Mughnī), the Benefactor (An-Nāfiʿ), the Self-Sufficient (Aṣ-Ṣamad), not the remembrance of Hind and Lubnā in their sayings.
A people who with (their) weapons subdued their enemies, until they rose high with privileges and charisms.
The pillars of the house of all these people are four, upon which the edifice of sainthood is founded:
silence, long hunger, after it vigil, and seclusion (learned) from masters through their indications.
A people whose way shields the disciple from the harm of the Rebel (Satan) and from every kind of delusion.
Their way is to aim at the Face of Allah without passion, with the principles that banish the vanities of the ego.
(Principles) such as repentance placed first, fear and with it hope, the constant increase of sorrow, with contentment in little;
renunciation of all that perishes, and after it scrupulousness, with trusting reliance (on Allah) and patience at every hour;
striving against the soul, gratitude, contentment with the (divine) decree, ceasing to turn one's gaze to the state of creatures.
Their way has ten requisites, indispensable to those who possess aspiration:
the intent, which is what leads to the journey; among them the guide, such as a master endowed with (spiritual) openings;
the provision, which is God-fearing piety; among them their weapon, which is the ablution that removes impurities;
among them the lamp, through the remembrance of Allah – glorified and exalted is He –; among them the mounts, through lofty aspirations;
among them the staff, through (awareness of one's own) helplessness; and the belt, among the people of the Way, is resolve according to the realities;
and among its requisites is its road, for ever, which is the Sharīʿa, at the beginning and at the ends;
and companionship, which is brothers endowed with aspirations, with sincere loyalty in brotherhood.
And each among the whole company of masters, possessed of ranks, shields the disciple from a rebel full of errors.
Each of these people is a learned and scrupulous master; among them one who trains through invocations and (spiritual) states;
among them one who uplifts through the (spiritual) state alone, always; among them one who trains and uplifts through indications.
Each is expert in all the diseases of the hearts together, and shields the disciples from every kind of misery.
Each is noble, God-fearing, endowed with guidance and generosity; he dispenses sincere counsel among all creatures.
Through God-fearing piety he puts aside all the cravings of the soul; he takes in sublime sciences from the Lord.
He makes plain and clear the way of the people of Allah for all who seek guidance, through outpourings (of grace).
Each has an aspiration by which he ever ascends toward the Mighty (Al-ʿAzīz), the Giver of might (Al-Muʿizz), through (spiritual) openings.
He sees hidden things with the eye of the heart as manifest, just as he beholds what lies beneath the veils.
He holds a radiance like the light of the sun wherever he turns; every person seeking illumination is favoured by it.
